 Order

This writ petition has been filed seeking issuance of a writ of mandamus directing second respondent to re-determine the compensation awarded to petitioners' lands acquired at Karasur Revenue Village in Award No.2 of 2008, at Rs.21,261/- per are, based on the application under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 dated 20.03.2019 & 22.03.2019 and the representation dated 30.05.2024 pursuant to the enhanced compensation _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 04/09/2025 08:44:55 pm ) award passed in L.A.O.P.No.110 of 2012 on the file of II Additional District Judge, Puducherry.
2. By consent of learned counsel on both sides, this writ petition is taken up for final disposal at the admission stage itself.

3. The case of the petitioners is that petitioners' land was acquired for the purpose of setting up of Special Economic Zone by invoking urgency provision under Section 17(4) of Land Acquisition Act,
1894, by the first respondent based on the request made by fourth respondent and the notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act came to be published on 24.03.2005.
The acquisition proceeding was completed and petitioners received a communication dated 04.07.2006 conveying the offer of 80% of compensation in advance.
Petitioners produced all the relevant documents to prove the ownership and possession.
The final award came to be passed in Award No.2 of 2008 on 25.01.2008.
Aggrieved by quantum of compensation, one of the land owner preferred an Reference Application _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 04/09/2025 08:44:55 pm ) seeking enhancement of compensation.
Reference Application was taken on file as L.A.O.P.No.110 of 2012.
The said LAOP was disposed of by enhancing the compensation and granting 30% Solatium and 12% Additional Market Value.
Based on the said award in L.A.O.P.No.110 of 2012, petitioners made an application under Section 28(A) to second respondent seeking to redetermine the compensation awarded to his lands.
However, respondents have not come forward to consider the application and therefore, petitioners filed the present petition.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned Additional Government Pleader (Puducherry) appearing for respondents that action has already been initiated vide Letter No.622/DCRS/SEZ/B3/2025 dated 07.07.2025 and the same holds good for the present petitioners also with regard to sanction and disbursement of the enhanced compensation under Section 28A of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The said statement is recorded.

The relevant portion of the proceedings dated 07.07.2025 is extracted hereunder:

_ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

5. Learned counsel for petitioners would only request that the application of petitioners may be considered within a specified time to be fixed by this Court to which learned Additional Government Pleader would submit that they would do so as expeditiously as possible.

6. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case and the stand taken by learned Additional Government Pleader (Puducherry), there shall be a direction to the concerned respondent to consider Section 28(A) application submitted by petitioners and pass appropriate orders within a period of four months from the date of uploading of the web copy without waiting for the receipt of certified copy.

It is made clear that this Court has not expressed any view with regard to the merits of the case and it is open to the concerned respondent to consider the matter on its own merits and in accordance with law. _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
7. With the above direction, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
No costs.
